scope: Theorem 3.9 (Extreme upper amplitude) of the manuscript “Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level” (preprints/Ramanujan-Arthur-Decompositions-of-Cuspidal-Functions-at-Full-Finite-Level-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 014 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b4b0cfe23007d159), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the finite Koszul specialization at [t] of K(V ⊠d µ ), retain the part with maximal absolute value for the d-fold slide at the chosen leg. Its cohomological upper bound is C + max e∈Et d⟨µ, he⟩. (3.5) The constant is independent of m. It is also uniform when t is replaced by tz, with z ∈ Z( b G)◦, after omitting the absolute-value central part, and when one chooses among a fixed finite list of hyperspecial variants. Fixed additional kernels at disjoint places are permitted. Unless t, modulo its absolute-value central part, is a compact factor times a Jacobson– Morozov point for Q, the difference between 2d⟨λ, µ⟩ and the nonconstant term in Equa- tion (3.5) is positive and grows linearly with m.
